scope: Primary-source review of controlled language, compositional semantics, constrained decoding and formal synthesis; no source-to-clinical-formula accuracy claims transferred from code or general-language benchmarks.

sources.title: Discourse Representation Structures for ACE 6.7 / Attempto Parsing Engine
sources.primary_type: Author technical report and official language/parser documentation
sources.representation: Nested DRS with typed predicate arguments, implication/disjunction, classical negation, explicit modal extensions; FOL/PNF/TPTP exports for supported representations.
sources.method: A precisely controlled input language fixes coordination, quantifier scope and reference interpretation; parser compiles that language and exposes paraphrases and source sentence/token anchors.
sources.verification_guarantee: Unambiguous interpretation relative to ACE rules for accepted ACE text; deterministic compiler/export behavior is distinct from an LLM translation claim.
sources.not_guaranteed: Arbitrary guideline-to-ACE fidelity, intended clinical scope, author intent, corpus completeness. ACE 6.7 modal/negation-as-failure extensions must not all be mislabeled ordinary FOL.
sources.evaluation: Specification examples and executable parser interface, not a held-out arbitrary-guideline extraction accuracy benchmark.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Reference for audited controlled paraphrases, predicate/role/source anchors and distinguishing logical negation from failure-to-prove; adaptation requires independent source-to-paraphrase adjudication.

source_locations.supports: nested operators, distinct negations, source sentence/token numbers, cardinality scope

sources.title: Minimal Recursion Semantics: An Introduction
sources.primary_type: Author-hosted research paper, supplemented by author research and official ERG documentation
sources.representation: Elementary predications plus handles, quantifier bound variables, restrictor/body and scope constraints; underspecified predicate calculus with generalized quantifiers, not merely an unordered triple set.
sources.method: Compositional grammar preserves semantic arguments while factoring out scope into explicit links; unresolved scope can denote multiple compatible readings.
sources.verification_guarantee: Representation preserves constraints under the specified compositional formalism; it permits reconstructing scope instead of erasing it.
sources.not_guaranteed: Correct selection of the intended reading from arbitrary clinical prose; fully resolved scope from syntax alone; reduction of all generalized quantifiers to ordinary FOL.
sources.evaluation: Formal representation/composition analysis and integration with broad-coverage HPSG; no reported universal clinical extraction score.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Strong counterexample to predicate-bag extraction; domains, roles and scope links must survive any flat storage. Preserving ambiguity is preferable to inventing a unique clinical scope.

source_locations.supports: scope-erased forms confound different universal statements; scope underspecification and restrictor/body
RMRS argument underspecification, algebra constraints and need for a grammar checker
ARG0/RSTR/BODY, syntactically partial scope, generalized quantifiers including most

sources.title: Wide-Coverage Semantic Analysis with Boxer
sources.representation: CCG-derived DRS, event variables and thematic roles, with FOL translation.
sources.method: Lexical semantics plus compositional derivation, followed by separate anaphora/presupposition resolution.
sources.verification_guarantee: Produces formally interpretable representations for accepted parses; it does not certify the parse or lexical interpretation.
sources.not_guaranteed: Source faithfulness, coreference, measurement interpretation or coordination scope; author explicitly reports failures.
sources.evaluation: >95% newswire coverage and complete DRSs for seven shared-task texts; authors explicitly lack gold representations to quantify semantic quality.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Useful component separation and event-role representation; coverage must not be reported as fidelity. Clinical causation/passive-role cases need their own validation.

source_locations.supports: composition, unresolved pronouns, role successes, measurement failures and unavailable gold accuracy
official PMB identifies Boxer as its CCG-to-DRS component; original historical C&C source URL was not revalidated as a live download

sources.title: The Parallel Meaning Bank: Towards a Multilingual Corpus of Translations Annotated with Compositional Meaning Representations
sources.primary_type: Primary corpus/system paper and official data documentation
sources.representation: Compositional DRS with layered tokenization, CCG syntax, semantic tags and normalized symbols.
sources.method: Automatic annotation plus persistent human corrections; conflicts with previously checked annotations are sent to expert re-adjudication.
sources.verification_guarantee: Explicit human-verification status and correction provenance; gold, silver and bronze do not denote the same evidence quality.
sources.not_guaranteed: Automatic DRS correctness; bilingual alignment always preserving meaning; generalization to multi-page clinical lists.
sources.evaluation: 2017 corpus construction/annotation counts. Official current data page lists v5.1.0 English gold=11,987 (2024-04-25), not an automatic extractor accuracy.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Source-first adjudicated rule units and reviewed-vs-machine-only status are supported by a mature semantic annotation workflow; operator/domain conflicts need targeted review.

sources.title: PICARD: Parsing Incrementally for Constrained Auto-Regressive Decoding from Language Models
sources.primary_type: Primary EMNLP paper and authors' code repository
sources.representation: SQL AST under lexical, grammar and table/alias scope guards.
sources.method: Incremental parser rejects inadmissible tokens during beam search; guards use declared database schema and symbol scope.
sources.verification_guarantee: Constraints implemented by parser/guards on successfully completed parses; output may still fail if beam search finds no valid completion.
sources.not_guaranteed: Correct query intent, source implication direction, all type checks, or faithful clinical interpretation. Paper leaves further type guards to future work.
sources.evaluation: T5-3B Spider development execution errors 12%→2%; exact-set match=75.5%, execution match=79.3%; these are separate endpoints.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Evidence for recursive syntax and binding guards. A syntactically valid excludes rule can still reverse the source; decoder constraints alone cannot adjudicate that.

sources.title: Synchromesh: Reliable Code Generation from Pre-trained Language Models
sources.primary_type: Primary ICLR paper and Microsoft Research publication page
sources.code_status: No author-maintained implementation link established from the primary paper/publication page; the retrieved kanishkg/synchromesh repository explicitly labels itself unofficial and was not used as primary implementation evidence.
sources.representation: SQL, Vega-Lite and SMCalFlow programs with completion engines enforcing syntax, scope, types and context-specific constraints.
sources.method: Constrained Semantic Decoding plus examples retrieved by target AST similarity (TST). Guarantees are relative to implemented completion-engine constraints.
sources.verification_guarantee: Completed generated programs satisfy the CE constraints under the stated CE axioms/decoding assumptions.
sources.not_guaranteed: Conceptual fidelity to natural-language intent; §4.2 explicitly supplies a valid-but-wrong visualization counterexample. Original domains are not Turing-complete Python.
sources.evaluation: Table2 Codex175B SQL CSD+TST: validity85%, execution match64%; SMCalFlow validity99%, exact match63%. Validity is not intent correctness.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Typed/domain-aware completion and examples selected by logical form are relevant; neither certifies which connective or implication the guideline intended.

source_locations.supports: AST example similarity, constraint guarantee, measured validity/accuracy split, explicit conceptual-error and language-scope limits
author/team provenance, target languages and public paper link

sources.title: Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models
sources.primary_type: Primary PLDI paper and authors' reproduction package
sources.representation: Simply typed language LB and TypeScript implementation using prefix automata and a type environment.
sources.method: Type search checks whether a partial expression can still be completed to an expression of the required type, beyond grammar-only masking.
sources.verification_guarantee: Sound well-typed completion for the covered language subset and completed generation; the formal construction intentionally sacrifices completeness for type-search termination.
sources.not_guaranteed: All TypeScript features, higher-order type completeness, functional correctness or correspondence to natural-language specifications. Prefix completable does not guarantee that the LLM terminates or stays within token/time budgets; §6 reports loops/truncations among remaining compiler errors.
sources.evaluation: TypeScript HumanEval/MBPP synthesis, translation and repair; paper reports compilation errors reduced by more than half and relative functional-correctness gains3.5%–5.5% for synthesis/translation.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Domain/role/quantity typing can rule out impossible bindings but not a well-typed donor/recipient swap or valid-yet-reversed logical rule.

source_locations.supports: syntax-vs-type distinction, prefix completion, intentionally incomplete covered subset and empirical endpoints; distinction between prefix-completion guarantee and actual generation termination
actual parser interface, incomplete-prefix examples and reproduction package

sources.title: Combinatorial Sketching for Finite Programs
sources.primary_type: Primary ASPLOS research paper and author code repository
sources.representation: Finite programs with holes plus a separate formal executable specification; synthesis problem uses bounded input semantics.
sources.method: Two SAT solvers alternate synthesis and verification; a violating input becomes a new synthesis constraint until the formal specification is met.
sources.verification_guarantee: Correctness relative to the supplied formal specification and finite domain; theoretical completion for a realizable sketch within the finite setup.
sources.not_guaranteed: That the formal specification faithfully captures an English guideline; unbounded/general-purpose correctness or practical termination within any fixed budget.
sources.evaluation: Finite programming kernels including AES; not text-to-FOL extraction or clinical diagnosis.
sources.transfer_to_repo: Counterexamples can discriminate candidate formula/executor variants only when an independently grounded reference behavior or specification exists; a self-generated specification can certify its own mistake.

source_locations.supports: formal-specification boundary, synthesize-verify counterexamples and bounded-domain guarantee

source_locations.location: Repository docs/SketchManual, benchmarks, source and README
source_locations.supports: author-associated implementation availability; no claim of reproducing it in this audit

sources.title: LogicNG: Normal Form Transformations
sources.representation: Propositional formula trees, NNF/CNF/DNF, auxiliary-variable encodings.
sources.method: Separate equivalent factorization from Tseitin/Plaisted-Greenbaum equisatisfiable transforms; preserve subformula definitions for SAT-oriented compilation.
sources.verification_guarantee: Truth-equivalent transformation or equisatisfiability as specified by the selected algorithm, assuming the input formula is correct. For full definitional Tseitin encoding with an asserted root, phi(x) iff exists z T(x,z), preserving models projected onto original variables; this is stronger than equisatisfiability alone.
sources.not_guaranteed: Source-to-formula fidelity; equisatisfiability alone is not pointwise equivalence over all original and auxiliary variable assignments.
sources.evaluation: Algorithm specification and worked examples; no extraction performance experiment.
sources.transfer_to_repo: CNF/DNF need not be the extraction surface form. Retain source AST/graph; canonicalization can be a downstream operation, with auxiliary-variable semantics explicit.

source_locations.location: CNF Transformations; CNF Factorization; Tseitin Transformation; Plaisted-Greenbaum Transformation
